Question: What appears in the terminal after each command? What does args[] contain when Average runs?

Concept under consideration: standard_input

Candidate edges of this concept. A misconception/error edge shows the wrong rule (logic) and the right rule (twin_logic); a concept edge shows the rule that links the two concepts.
- err:standard_input->StdLibraryNotInDirectory | wrong rule: Uses StdIn (or StdDraw/StdAudio) without StdIn.java in the working directory. | right rule: The Std* libraries are not built into Java; StdIn.java etc. must be in the same directory (or on the classpath), otherwise Java reports NoClassDefFoundError.
- mis:standard_input->NextLineAfterNextInt | wrong rule: A line read after a number read returns the next line typed. | right rule: The number read leaves the newline, so the line read returns "" unless the newline is consumed first.
- mis:standard_input->RereadIntoVariableInvalid | wrong rule: Reading a second input value into a variable that already holds one is an error, so the program cannot run. | right rule: A later read simply overwrites the variable's current value.
- mis:standard_input->StdInRereads | wrong rule: Calling StdIn.readInt() twice returns the same value twice. | right rule: The program consumes values when it reads them, so each call returns the next value.
- err:standard_input->InputTypeMismatch | wrong rule: StdIn.readInt() accepts any typed text such as abc or 12.2. | right rule: If the next token is not an int (e.g. abc, 12.2, true), StdIn.readInt() throws a NumberFormatException at run time (Scanner.nextInt throws InputMismatchException).
- err:standard_input->ReadPastEndOfInput | wrong rule: Calls StdIn.readInt() again after the input has run out. | right rule: Reading after standard input is exhausted is a run-time error; test StdIn.isEmpty() before each read.
- mis:standard_input->InputReadOnceBeforeLoop | wrong rule: Reading a value once before the loop is enough; the loop will process each new input value. | right rule: A read loop must read the next value inside the body on every pass; otherwise it keeps processing the same value.
